record.paper_title: Selected Old Open Problems in General Topology
record.original_question: Does there exist, in ZFC, a topological group that is extremally disconnected and non-discrete, where extremal disconnectedness means that the closure of every open subset is open?

evidence.quote: disconnected if the closure of every open subset of X is open.

Problem 9 (A. V. Arhangel’skii, 1967) . Construct in ZF C a non-discrete ex-
tremally disconnected topological group.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A topological space $X$ is called extremally disconnected if the closure of every open subset of $X$ is open. A topological group is a group $G$ equipped with a topology such that the multiplication map $G \times G \to G$ and the inversion map $G \to G$ are continuous. A topological space is discrete if every subset is open.

Working in ZFC (Zermelo–Fraenkel set theory with the axiom of choice, with no additional set-theoretic assumptions), determine whether there exists a Hausdorff topological group $G$ that is extremally disconnected and non-discrete.
artifact.status_search_result: Arhangel'skii's 1967 problem remains open in ZFC in general. Partial results: under additional set-theoretic axioms (e.g., Jensen's Diamond, or the existence of measurable cardinals / certain ultrafilters), nondiscrete extremally disconnected groups can be constructed. Reznichenko and Sipacheva (2021) showed that the existence of a countable nondiscrete extremally disconnected group implies the existence of a rapid ultrafilter, so such countable groups cannot be constructed in ZFC alone. The uncountable case in ZFC remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Discrete Subsets in Topological Groups and Countable Extremally Disconnected Groups
status_evidence.snippet: Existence of a countable nondiscrete extremally disconnected group implies the existence of a rapid ultrafilter.
status_evidence.claim: Countable case cannot be settled positively in ZFC alone.

status_evidence.title: Extremally Disconnected Groups of Measurable Cardinality
status_evidence.snippet: Existence of measurable cardinals implies nondiscrete extremally disconnected groups exist; ZFC case unclear.
status_evidence.claim: The ZFC problem (uncountable case) remains open.

status_evidence.title: A study of extremally disconnected topological spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Survey states Arhangel'skii's 1967 problem on a nondiscrete extremally disconnected topological group in ZFC remains unresolved.
